USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

gustilo — pattern 1

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

During operative assessment of an open tibial fracture, the surgeon finds a clean 5-mm puncture caused by a bone spike. The injury was low energy, contamination is minimal, and there is little soft-tissue damage without vascular injury. Which Gustilo–Anderson grade best describes the injury?

  1. Type IIIA
  2. Type IIIB
  3. Type IIIC
  4. Type I
  5. Type II
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Type I

Type I: A low-energy open fracture with a clean wound under 1 cm and minimal soft-tissue damage.

Understanding the options

Type I
Type I: A low-energy open fracture with a clean wound under 1 cm and minimal soft-tissue damage.
Type II
Type II describes an open fracture with a wound over 1 cm but without extensive soft-tissue destruction, flaps or avulsion. The case instead matches Type I.
Type IIIA
Type IIIA describes a severe open fracture with adequate viable soft-tissue coverage of the bone. The case instead matches Type I.
Type IIIB
Type IIIB describes an open fracture with extensive soft-tissue loss, periosteal stripping and inadequate bone coverage requiring flap reconstruction. The case instead matches Type I.
Type IIIC
Type IIIC describes an open fracture associated with an arterial injury requiring repair, regardless of wound size. The case instead matches Type I.
